title: Matthew 1:1
paragraphs: For what reason did he not say “a vision” or “a word,” as the prophets did? For those men would write at the outset thus: “A vision which Isaiah saw,”f1 and “The word that came to Isaiah.”f2 For what reason did he not? — do you seek to learn? Because the prophets, on the one hand, were conversing with people hard-hearted and disobedient, and for this reason they said that it is a divine vision and that it is a word from God, so that the people might be afraid and might not despise the things that were spoken. But Matthew, on the other hand, had to do with people who had believed, and who were well-disposed and obedient; and for this reason he said beforehand nothing of the sort, such as the prophets did.

But I have also something else to say: that the prophets, on the one hand, beheld intellectuallyf3 the things which they beheld, picturing these through the Holy Spirit — wherefore they also called these things “visions”; but Matthew, on the other hand, did not behold Christ intellectually and picture him, but was present with him perceptibly and heard him perceptibly, seeing him in the flesh.
